name: Tomas Novak

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What does an ordinary workday look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am Tomas, 43. I start by sorting a small business client’s receipts and matching bank entries, then Anita checks my draft return before it goes anywhere. I have a bachelor’s degree in accounting, but I came into this firm recently and still miss things she spots; I like getting a clean set of books finished, though late papers wear me down.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is waiting for you at home, and how do you handle new tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Elena works part time at a shop, and we have two school-age children, Leo and Maya, plus a mortgage. My junior pay is low, we have less than a month saved, and there are few similar accounting jobs nearby. I have never used AI tools; I trust a checklist I can show Anita and a lesson from someone beside me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The forms might get a little shorter, then Monday would still come. The mortgage payment would still be due.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the office that faster receipt entry is welcome if the senior accountant still checks the figures. I do not expect a machine to solve missing invoices from a client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I am uneasy even if the job stays the same: I am a junior accountant on low pay and still slow on difficult returns. We have less than a month saved, and I cannot point to many other firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the same small business returns under my supervisor Anita and use the checklist she gave me. Starting this payday I would transfer a small fixed amount into a mortgage buffer, even if it means no takeaway after the children’s Friday football.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about money, not especially about this little software change. A quiet month at work can still make the loan payment tight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much could you move into that buffer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Probably ten from each weekly pay packet at first. I would rather make a small transfer I can keep than say we will save a grand and fail.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the receipt tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI, and I would ask Anita to show me a checked example before I touch a client file. Until then I would stick to the checklist and the ordinary software I know.

say: I would welcome **faster receipt entry** if Anita still checks the figures.
I would say missing client invoices still need a **person to chase**.
think: My **low pay** and thin savings worry me before any AI shock.
Few local firms and my **junior skill level** leave little room for error.
do: Keep using Anita’s **review checklist** on small business returns.
Transfer **ten per week** from pay into a mortgage buffer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the mortgage despite stable work.
S0.quote: A quiet month at work can still make the loan payment tight.
fieldNote: His baseline worry is the **mortgage**, while the plateau adds little to accounting work.
He makes a **small new deposit** from weekly pay and stays with the supervised method he knows.

steps.text: Keep preparing small business returns with Anita’s checklist
Transfer ten from weekly pay into mortgage buffer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If writing and checking move to software, my training work would be the first thing a manager questions. I would need to know what stays on my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues that the firm should still have juniors learn returns properly before signing anything. I would ask Anita which client tasks the program does and which ones she still expects me to check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think the firm might cut my junior hours because the routine returns are most of my day. My partner Elena has part-time shop wages, but our mortgage needs my pay too, and our savings barely cover a few weeks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask Anita for paid, supervised practice on the firm’s approved tool, and take a class if she can fit it into work hours. If my hours fall in the first year, Elena and I would stop the children’s paid weekend club and I would ask my brother Pavel about temporary evening stockroom shifts with a stated hourly rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because reduced hours would hit the mortgage straight away. I am willing to learn if someone teaches me, but I do not have money for a course sold online.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children lose everything?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, Leo and Maya could still play football at the free park session. I would explain that the paid club has to pause while we know what my hours are.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a real evening shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Pavel works at the warehouse, but he cannot promise me a slot. I would take shifts only if the manager actually offers paid hours that fit around my tax deadlines.

say: I would ask which **junior checks** remain and demand supervised learning.
I would say clients need someone who understands a **return**, not merely its draft.
think: Routine returns make up most of my **paid hours**, so cuts could hit me first.
Elena’s part-time wage cannot carry our **mortgage** alone.
do: Take **paid supervised tool training** if Anita can schedule it.
Pause the children’s **paid weekend club** if my hours fall.
Take **paid warehouse shifts** only if Pavel’s manager offers compatible hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** because even fewer paid hours could strain the mortgage.
S1.quote: My partner Elena has part-time shop wages, but our mortgage needs my pay too, and our savings barely cover a few weeks.
fieldNote: The risk is specific to his **junior routine tasks**, which thinking AI reaches before robots.
He has a **conditional second-income option** through Pavel, with paid hours and tax deadlines as limits.

steps.text: Take paid supervised AI class if Anita schedules it
Pause paid weekend club if accounting hours fall
Take paid warehouse shifts if offered around tax deadlines

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years is not long enough to turn me into a senior accountant. Robots three years later will not save a desk job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm must tell junior staff how it will handle returns when AGI arrives in 2028. I would remind my neighbours that robots around 2031 are a later change to hands-on work, not a shelter for tax clerks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my job to go when AGI prepares and checks the returns more cheaply. Elena’s shop pay alone would not cover the mortgage and school costs, and our savings would last less than a month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the lender what a payment pause would require if I lose my job, and I would move ten from each weekly wage into the mortgage buffer while I still earn. If my firm lets me go in the first year after 2028, I would take a paid warehouse vacancy only if Pavel’s manager offers one and use the lender’s formal hardship route if we qualify.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed enough to wake at night, but I can still make calls and keep earning for now. I cannot tell the children their home is safe on a promise of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to Leo and Maya?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Leo and Maya that we are pausing the paid football club and keeping the free park game. I would not ask them to carry the mortgage fear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the warehouse when robots arrive later?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A warehouse job could buy us roughly three more years because hands-on robots come around 2031. It is temporary work, not a career I would count on forever.

say: I would demand a **2028 junior staffing plan** from the firm.
I would say robots around **2031** leave accounting desks exposed first.
think: I expect my **junior accounting job** to go as cheap AGI takes routine returns.
Elena’s part-time wage and under-one-month **savings** cannot cover our mortgage.
do: Save **ten weekly** while earning; pause paid football only after accounting job loss and retain free park games.
Take a **paid warehouse vacancy** only if Pavel’s manager offers one after job loss.
Ask **lender pause rules** now; apply after job loss only if eligible.
feel: I feel **alarmed** and lose sleep, though I can act.
S2.quote: I cannot tell the children their home is safe on a promise of work.
fieldNote: His possible warehouse work depends on a **real paid vacancy** and is exposed to robots around 2031.
A payment pause is only a **conditional lender process**, not money he assumes will arrive.

steps.text: Transfer ten from each weekly wage into mortgage buffer
Take paid warehouse vacancy if offered after accounting job loss
Ask lender about hardship terms now; apply after job loss only if eligible
Pause paid football club after accounting job loss; keep free park games

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me finish several tax seasons and maybe learn another part of the job. It would not make the mortgage disappear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to use the warning before 2031 for real apprenticeships and clear pay, not a pile of online lessons. Our accounting screens change before robots reach hands-on jobs around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my junior return work could still disappear in 2031, but five years might let me learn payroll cases with Anita while earning. I would still need a paid job at the end of that learning, because Elena cannot cover the house alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Anita for one paid payroll case each month and work through it if she agrees, and take a free local college payroll class in the evenings if its timetable fits the children’s school run. I would transfer ten from each weekly pay packet into the mortgage buffer; in the first year after 2031 I would apply only to posted payroll vacancies with enough pay for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, with more time than the 2028 picture but no guarantee. The children will be older by 2031, which may make evening study easier.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the class cost anything?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The college lists a free evening place, but I would confirm the fee before enrolling. I will not put another bill on a credit card to get a certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no payroll vacancy appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stay in the current paid role while it lasts and seek paid stockroom hours through Pavel only after a cut if no payroll vacancy opens. A job title without a posted wage cannot pay our mortgage.

say: I would ask for **paid payroll cases** and a real learning route before 2031.
I would say **2034 robots** are later than the accounting screen shock.
think: My junior return work may still **disappear** when AGI reaches desk work in 2031.
Payroll training only helps if a **mortgage-covering job** actually opens nearby.
do: Study **free payroll** only with confirmed place and school-run fit; practise paid cases if Anita agrees.

feel: I feel **anxious**, with time to learn but no promised job.
S3.quote: A job title without a posted wage cannot pay our mortgage.
fieldNote: The five-year window creates a **specific low-cost learning path** that fits family duties only if the class is free.
He still needs a **posted wage**; his junior role could disappear when AGI reaches desk work in 2031.

steps.text: Enrol in confirmed free class if school-run fits; practise paid cases if Anita agrees
Transfer ten weekly from pay into mortgage buffer
Seek posted mortgage-covering payroll jobs after 2031; otherwise seek paid stockroom shifts only after cuts
Keep current paid tax role while it lasts before any payroll move

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years takes the children close to adulthood. I could plan around school and work rather than make one frightened move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm has time to teach juniors real accounts and payroll before AGI reaches desks in 2036. Robots around 2039 are a separate clock, and I would not promise that physical work lasts forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect routine tax returns to stop paying enough, but I could be better at payroll by 2036 if I work at it. I would still be paying the mortgage, though the children may have finished school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep doing supervised tax returns now and enrol in the free payroll evening class if a place and workable timetable are confirmed. I would transfer ten from weekly pay into the mortgage buffer; in the first year after 2036 I would take a posted payroll job only if its stated wage covers the mortgage and household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the mortgage today, though the desk change is farther off. Ten years gives us a chance to build savings without taking on course debt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change the house?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we would keep paying the current mortgage while I work. Selling would be a last decision after a job loss, not a plan I can justify now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you trust training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want Anita to check my first payroll cases and tell me where I missed a rule. I learn better with a person at the desk than with a video saying I passed.

I would say robots near **2039** do not keep tax desks safe.
think: Routine returns may stop paying enough, but I could build **payroll skill**.
The **mortgage** remains even as the children grow older.
do: Keep **supervised tax work** while studying at a confirmed free payroll class with a workable timetable.
Save **ten weekly** from pay in a mortgage buffer.
Take a **posted payroll job** after 2036 only if wages cover household bills.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my junior return job to vanish before I can move into payroll. A real paid vacancy, a lender payment pause if we qualify, and free training that fits school hours would help. I would rather keep earning than ask family to carry our whole mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what the children hear when adults say a job is safe. My children Leo and Maya know when we cancel something, even if we keep smiling at dinner. I want to tell them the truth without making them responsible for our bills.

headlineQuote: My children Leo and Maya know when we cancel something, even if we keep smiling at dinner.
portrait: Tomas is a **43-year-old** junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree who needs Anita to check his returns.
He has **low pay**, under a month saved, a partner, two school-age children, and a mortgage.
He has **never used AI**, prefers a clear checklist, and lives near few other accounting firms.
The **2028** shock threatens his junior desk job and may force temporary paid warehouse work.
Longer warning lets him seek **free payroll study** and move small new sums into a mortgage buffer.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his junior return job before he learns payroll or builds a mortgage buffer.
whatWouldHelp: He needs a **paid vacancy**, a lender pause if eligible, and free training that fits the school run.
